tasks.title: TrieRouter breaks when a regexp param spans 3+ path parts
grep resolves a symlinked search root to its real path
revert and fork select messages by ID comparison instead of position

runs.output:
I'll find the RPC client cookie serialization code.`src/client/client.ts:98-104` — root cause: the RPC client built the request `Cookie` header with `serialize(key, value, { path: '/' })` (the *response* `Set-Cookie` serializer) and joined pairs with `,`.

Fix: emit bare `name=value` pairs, joined with `; `.

```ts
if (args?.cookie) {
  const cookies: string[] = []
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(args.cookie)) {
    cookies.push(`${key}=${encodeURIComponent(value)}`)
  }
  headerValues['Cookie'] = cookies.join('; ')
}
```

- No `Path=/` (or any `Set-Cookie` attribute) leaks into the request header.
- `; ` delimiter matches RFC 6265 §5.4, so the server's `parse()` reads every pair — `hello=world; goodbye=moon`.
- Value still `encodeURIComponent`-encoded, matching `tryDecodeURIComponent` on the parse side.
- Dropped the now-unused `serialize` import from `../utils/cookie`.

Verified: `tsc --noEmit` passes; `src/client/client.test.ts` 104/104 pass. The `types.test.ts` / `jsx` type-test failures in `bun run test` are pre-existing and unrelated.

runs.output:
I'll start by examining the TrieRouter implementation.`src/router/trie-router/node.ts:203` — `m[0].match(/\//)` used a non-global regex. `String.prototype.match` without `/g` returns a match array of length 1 (the first match plus capture groups), so `componentCount` was always `0` or `1`, never the actual number of slashes consumed by the regexp match.

`componentCount` is how many extra path parts the multi-part param swallowed; it schedules the child node into `curNodesQueue[componentCount]` so it resumes at the right depth. Under-counting shifted the resume point too early:

- **Symptom 1** — `/:dirs{.+}/file.html` against `/a/b/c/d/file.html`: match spans 3 slashes, counted as 1 → node resumed at part index 1 instead of 3 → `file.html` child never reached → 404. Depths 1–2 worked because the true count was ≤ 1.
- **Symptom 2** — `/:file{.*}/*` against `/a/b/c`: regex consumes the whole rest, handler pushed once via the `m[0].length === restPathString.length` branch. Count 2 → 1 requeued the node at part `c`, where its `'*'` pattern fired and pushed the same handler a second time.

Fix — one character:

```ts
const componentCount = m[0].match(/\//g)?.length ?? 0
```

`null ?? 0` still covers the zero-slash case. Verified: all four `/:dirs{.+}/file.html` paths now 200 with correct `dirs` param, raw `TrieRouter` returns the handler once, middleware `runs === 1`. Full suite green (146 files / 4744 tests). Pre-existing type errors in `src/client/client.test.ts` and `src/jsx/*` are unrelated and untouched.

I'll find the grep tool implementation first.`packages/opencode/src/tool/grep.ts:60` — `FSUtil.resolve(requested)` realpath'd the search root before running ripgrep. Removed.

Root cause: `FSUtil.resolve` → `realpathSync`, so `cwd` became the symlink target. Every match row is built as `path.resolve(cwd, item.entry.path)`, so results were reported under `/tmp/demo/real/…` instead of the requested `/tmp/demo/alias/…` — a path the caller never named, and outside the root the external-directory grant was scoped to.

Fix: search root is now the caller's path, lexically normalized only (`path.resolve` on the requested path — collapses `.`/`..`, leaves symlinks intact). `fs.stat` is now called once on `requested` and reused for both the external-directory `kind` and the file/dir `cwd` decision, dropping the duplicate stat on the resolved path. This matches `glob.ts`, which never realpath'd its search root.

Verified: repro (`alias` → `real`, file containing `needle`) now reports `…/alias/test.txt`, and the external-directory prompt is raised against the alias glob. `bun test test/tool/` — 338 pass, 0 fail. No tests written or modified.

runs.output:
I'll find the revert and fork logic.Root cause: three cut points selected messages by lexicographic ID comparison instead of by position in the already-ordered message list. `Session.messages()` returns messages ordered by `(time_created, id)`, so creation order is correct in the array — only the ID ordering is unreliable.

Fixed:

- `packages/opencode/src/session/revert.ts:74` — diff range was `all.filter((msg) => msg.info.id >= rev.messageID)`. Now locates the boundary by identity (`findIndex(id === rev.messageID)`) and slices the tail.
- `packages/opencode/src/session/revert.ts:106` — `cleanup` classified each message with `id < messageID` / `id > messageID`. Now finds the boundary index; everything at/after it is removed (the boundary message itself is kept as `target` when `partID` is set, preserving part-level trim semantics). Messages before the boundary are untouched.
- `packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts:705` — `fork` broke out of the copy loop on `msg.info.id >= input.messageID`. Now copies `msgs.slice(0, boundary)`; when no `messageID` is given (or it isn't in the session) the whole session is copied, as before.

Typecheck passes.
